title: Assessing readiness for transfer to adult care in adolescents with long-term conditions: a narrative review
subtitle: Interpretive narrative review to inform a transition clinic's readiness assessment
statement: A children's hospital uses a 20-item readiness questionnaire to decide when adolescents with long-term conditions transfer to adult care, but high scorers sometimes disengage after transfer and low scorers are kept in paediatrics against their wishes. The transition steering group needs a narrative review of what readiness tools measure, whether readiness scores predict outcomes after transfer, and how young people and families experience assessment, including young people with learning disabilities and families with low health literacy.
whoAffected: About 400 young people a year aged 14 to 19 with type 1 diabetes, inflammatory bowel disease, epilepsy, cystic fibrosis and other conditions; their families; paediatric and adult teams; the transition steering group.
whatHurts: A score used as a gate can delay transfer for young people who are ready and let others transfer without the support they need, and it may disadvantage young people with learning disabilities or low health literacy.
currentPractice: A 20-item self-report questionnaire at 14, 16 and 17.5 years, with the score informally used to time transfer.
whyNow: The steering group is revising the readiness assessment and meets in January 2027.
constraints: Two protected sessions a week for ten weeks (November 2026 to January 2027) plus support from the transition nurse specialist. Published literature only; no new data from patients. Report to the transition steering group in January 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Young people move to adult care when they and their families are ready, with support that fits their abilities and circumstances.
summary: Problem framed as an interpretive narrative review to inform a revised readiness assessment.
